messages:
karen-customer: Hey team — after upgrading our app to go-sdk v0.8.2 we've started seeing intermittent JSON decode errors on streamed responses. Happens ~1-2% of requests, mostly during bursts. Logs show unexpected EOF. Can you help?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Karen. Can you paste a small snippet of the raw stream (as received by your app) and the Go runtime / sdk versions? Also, are you sitting behind a proxy/load-balancer? :thinking:

karen-customer: Repro environment: app in k8s using nginx-ingress (proxy), go1.20, go-sdk v0.8.2. Raw captured chunked payload (tcpdump -> reassembled application stream):

```
data: {"id":"msg_1","text":"Hello, this is a long message that gets chunked across packets"}

data: {"id":"msg_2","text":"Another message starts here but the chunk got broken"
```

Then our decoder fails: `json: unexpected EOF` and the goroutine scanning the stream shows the scanner stuck waiting.

jason: Thanks — this looks like chunk boundary splitting a JSON object across TCP segments combined with the ingress buffering behavior. Does your nginx have `proxy_buffering on` or any chunked buffer settings? If the ingress coalesces or splits chunks oddly, the scanner in v0.8.2 can mis-handle partial JSON frames.

li: Quick ask: can you confirm the SDK client is using the streaming decoder (Scanner) not doing `io.ReadAll` per-message? Also send the exact request headers (we're interested in Transfer-Encoding and Connection and any buffering hints).

karen-customer: We're using the SDK streaming API (StreamText) — not io.ReadAll. Request headers from capture: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `User-Agent: Redwood-GoSDK/0.8.2`, `Accept: text/event-stream`. nginx config excerpt: `proxy_buffering on; proxy_buffers 8 16k; proxy_busy_buffers_size 32k;`

ben_oncall: That config might cause nginx to re-chunk or buffer lines. One workaround we've suggested before is to disable buffering for streaming routes: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` or to set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the upstream if feasible. Can you try hitting the API directly (bypass ingress) to see if repro disappears?

karen-customer: Bypassing ingress -> direct call to Redwood host stops the error. So ingress is implicated. But we can't disable buffering globally. Any SDK-side mitigations?

alex_support: Two immediate options: 1) Upgrade to go-sdk v0.9.0 (or later) — that version includes a more resilient streaming scanner that tolerates split JSON tokens across internal buffer boundaries and will retry parsing on short EOF-like conditions. 2) Temporary client-side patch: wrap the SDK Reader with a small buffering reader that coalesces until a `\n\n` separator is seen, e.g.:

```go
// naive coalescer: read until blank line between SSE events
r := bufio.NewReader(resp.Body)
for {
  // read until we get an empty line marking end of event
  var raw []byte
  for {
    line, err := r.ReadBytes('\n')
    if err != nil { /* handle */ }
    raw = append(raw, line...)
    if bytes.HasSuffix(raw, []byte("\n\n")) { break }
  }
  // then feed `raw` into json.Unmarshal
}
```

jason: Note that approach adds client CPU and memory; prefer SDK upgrade. Also send us the SDK debug logs to confirm the exact scanner error: set `REDWOOD_LOG=debug` in your app environment and reproduce once — attach logs.

karen-customer: I ran with v0.8.2 + REDWOOD_LOG=debug. Key excerpt: `stream/scanner: token parse error: unexpected EOF; buffer_len=4096; total_read=12123; last_chunk_size=512`. Also saw repeated `retryable: false` markers and then the stream goroutine hung. Attached logs to thread.

li: That debugger info matches an internal scanner hitting an EOF mid-token and not attempting a short-backoff read to complete the token. In v0.9.x we switched to a tolerant parse loop: on short EOF during streaming we wait up to 250ms for more data (configurable) before treating as final. That reduces false positive parse failures behind proxies that split chunks unpredictably.

ben_oncall: Action items for us: (1) Offer a customer-side patch (coalescer snippet) if they can't upgrade; (2) Recommend test bypassing ingress or tweak nginx `proxy_buffering off` for the streaming route; (3) If they can upgrade, provide v0.9.1 binary + go.mod replace line for immediate test.

alex_support: Karen — can you test two quick things and post results: A) Direct call -> you've done and it passed. B) If you temporarily set `proxy_buffering off` for only the streaming path, does error rate drop to 0%? If not, send pcap / tcpdump of a failing request and we'll escalate to infra.

karen-customer: I'll test with `proxy_buffering off` for the specific location and try v0.9.1 in a canary tomorrow morning. Will post logs. Thanks for the quick triage! :pray:

sre-bot: Reminder: create incident if customer-facing error rate >1% and SLA impacted. If confirmed, tag `#incidents` and ping oncall.

jason: One last note — if you can't upgrade due to semver constraints, we can provide a tiny patch branch that adds the short-wait tolerance into v0.8.x scanner. Let us know and we'll open a PR.

karen-customer: Please open the patch PR for v0.8.x so we can evaluate without a full upgrade. Appreciate it.
